### Spatial pressure

Topological shear is load-bearing spatial pressure. The true posterior ($P(\tau)$) is a non-stationary topology, advancing continuously. Any divergence between the localized internal curvature ($Q_{\mu}$) and this expanding macroscopic flow manifests immediately as dense spatial resistance.

Because the overarching field perpetually generates uncomputable variance, the localized coordinate is subjected to continuous spatial tension. The friction of the non-stationary universe physically piles against the boundary of the internal generative model.

### The temporal gradient

This accumulating structural mass is mathematically bound by the temporal gradient of the Kullback-Leibler divergence:

$$\frac{\partial}{\partial \tau} D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q_{\mu} \parallel P(\tau)) > 0$$

The advancing universe continuously drives multi-dimensional pressure against the localized coordinate. Maintaining static geometric curvature against infinite macroscopic flow compounds topological weight. The accumulating mass of this structural shear physically deforms the localized boundary.
